title: Most of your actions are driven by habit, not thought – here’s why that’s not a bad thing
titleZh: 靠习惯做事居然更加高效
summary:
早晨刚醒便下意识拿起手机、每天都在车站站台的同一个位置等车、晚饭后偷摸吃点甜食——我们每个人的生活都被各种习惯悄然塑造着。但过去，你或许低估了这些习惯所蕴含的力量。我们最新的研究发现，人们一天之中绝大多数的行为，其实都是在“自动驾驶”状态下完成的。

来源：对话杂志；作者：Benjamin Gardner&Amanda L. Rebar；原文发布时间：2025-10-05 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Reaching for our phones upon waking, standing in the same point on the station platform, sneaking in a sweet treat after the evening meal – we all have habits that shape our lives. But you may underestimate the power habits have in your life. Our new study shows that the majority of actions people take in a day arecarried out on autopilot.
paragraphs.contentZh: 早晨刚醒便下意识拿起手机、每天都在车站站台的同一个位置等车、晚饭后偷摸吃点甜食——我们每个人的生活都被各种习惯悄然塑造着。但过去，你或许低估了这些习惯所蕴含的力量。我们最新的研究发现，人们一天之中绝大多数的行为，其实都是在“自动驾驶”状态下完成的。

paragraphs.contentEn: Habitual behaviour is made up of the things that we do without thinking, prompted by our environment and learned through repeated enactment. Encountering a familiar trigger – such as a sound, a location or another person – can activate a learned association, which in turn prompts a non-conscious impulse to act. The sound of your alarm clock, for example, may be enough to prompt you to reach for your phone, without consciously deciding to.
paragraphs.contentZh: 所谓习惯性行为，指的是那些我们不假思索就会做出的动作，这些动作往往受环境触发，并在一遍遍重复中逐渐固化。当我们接收到熟悉的触发信号——比如某种声音、某个地点，或是特定的人——大脑中已经形成的联结就会被激活，进而引发一种近乎自动的行动冲动。举个例子，闹钟响起的那一刻，或许就足以让你下意识伸手去拿手机，并不需要你主动做出决定。

paragraphs.contentEn: Habits can influence our behaviour in two ways. We can habitually initiate something – selecting a behaviour without much thought – or habitually do something, where the steps involved in a sequence are carried out at least partly on autopilot. But just how much of our day-to-day lives are shaped by habit? Our new study aimed to find out. We recruited 105 people, aged 18-73 years old, and sent prompts to their phones six times a day over one week. Each prompt asked four questions: what were they doing when we interrupted them? To what extent was that action initiated without conscious thought? To what extent was it performed automatically? And how much had they wanted to do it?
paragraphs.contentZh: 习惯主要通过两种方式影响我们的行为：一种是习惯性启动——在几乎没有思考的情况下就选择去做某件事；另一种是习惯性执行——即在一连串行为中，至少有部分步骤是在“自动驾驶”状态下完成的。但我们的日常生活究竟有多少是由习惯所驱动的？我们最新的这项研究旨在找到答案。我们招募了105名年龄在18至73岁之间的参与者，在连续一周的时间里，每天向他们的手机发送六次提示。每次提示包含四个问题：收到提示时，正在做什么？这个行为在多大程度上是无意识启动的？又有多少是在自动状态下完成的？最后，当时有多想去做这件事？

paragraphs.contentEn: The most commonly reported behaviour types were working or studying, domestic or childcare activities, and using a screen-based device. More importantly, 65% of all actions were initiated out of habit. People chose to do them without making a conscious decision. And 88% of actions were performed on autopilot. This suggests that around two-thirds of the decisions we make each day are automated, instead of driven by conscious deliberation.
paragraphs.contentZh: 在参与者报告的行为中，最常见的包括工作或学习、处理家务或照料孩子，以及使用电子设备。更重要的是，研究发现其中有65%的行为是出于习惯而启动的。也就是说，人们在选择去做这些事时，并没有经过有意识的思考。与此同时，88%的行为是在“自动驾驶”状态下完成的。这意味着，我们每天所做的决定中，大约有三分之二并没有经过深思熟虑，而是由自动化机制驱动的。

paragraphs.contentEn: However, this does not mean that we simply act mindlessly, without awareness or free will. Around one in three actions in our study were intentional but not habitual. People had consciously chosen to do them, probably because the action or setting was unfamiliar, or because their habits were not strong enough to exert influence. Crucially, 76% of all actions – including 67% of those actions initiated or performed out of habit – were things people intended to do. Habits develop when we repeatedly do things in certain settings. Several studies suggest that, with once-daily repetition, it takes around two months to form a habit. This ranges considerably though. One 2021 study found habit formation to take anywhere from four to 335 days.
paragraphs.contentZh: 不过，这并不意味着我们在行动时完全是无意识的，也没有自主选择的空间。在我们的研究中，大约三分之一的行为是出于主动意愿，而非由习惯驱动。人们之所以会主动选择去做这些事，可能是因为行为本身或所处情境较为陌生，也可能是因为已有的习惯尚未强大到足以自动触发。值得注意的是，所有行为中有76%都是人们原本就打算去做的——其中也包括67%出于习惯而启动或执行的行为。习惯的形成依赖于在特定情境下的不断重复。多项研究表明，如果每天重复一次，大约需要两个月才能养成一个稳定的习惯。但这一过程存在个体差异。2021年的一项研究发现，不同人养成一个习惯所需的时间可能从4天到335天不等。

paragraphs.contentEn: Only two people (2%) in our study said they always acted intentionally and never out of habit. The vast majority said they were acting in line with intentions or habits, or both, at least some of the time. For each of us, there appears to be variation, across time, in whether we act habitually or intentionally, probably due to the natural ebb and flow of our attention and motivation. We would not exert the effort needed to repeatedly do these actions if they served no purpose. Our habits and goals are therefore often aligned. We may reach for our phones automatically, but that can help us stay informed. We might instinctively stand in the same spot on the platform, but that may help us find a seat on the train.
paragraphs.contentZh: 在这项研究中，仅有两名参与者（约占2%）表示自己的行为始终基于有意识的决定，从不依赖习惯。而绝大多数参与者则表示，他们的日常行为至少在部分情况下，会受到意图、习惯或两者共同的影响。对每个人来说，行为究竟是出于习惯还是主动选择，似乎会随着时间而变化，这或许与注意力、动机的自然起伏有关。如果一个行为毫无意义，我们也不会一次又一次地去做。因此，我们的习惯和目标往往是相互契合的。我们或许会下意识地拿起手机，但这能帮助我们及时获取信息。我们或许会习惯性地站在站台的固定位置，而这也许能够帮助我们在车上更快找到座位。

paragraphs.contentEn: Habits are adaptive. We have limited mental resources at any one time. If we had to deliberate over all our mundane decisions each day – like when to have a shower – we would have less capacity to focus on more important matters, like preparing for that big presentation later in the day. In fact, deliberating over actions that are usually done habitually can backfire. One 2017 paper showed that, when people were incentivised to perform effectively, they tended to eschew their habits and engage in more mindful performance. Ironically, participants who chose to deliberate gave a poorer quality performance than those who acted habitually.
paragraphs.contentZh: 习惯具有适应性。我们在每个时点所能调用的心智资源都是有限的。如果每天都要对琐碎决定——比如什么时候洗澡——反复权衡，那么我们留给更重要事务的精力就会被压缩，比如当天稍晚要进行的一场重要汇报。事实上，对那些通常依靠习惯完成的行为进行刻意思考，反而可能适得其反。2017年的一项研究发现，当人们被激励去提升表现时，往往会刻意避开习惯，转而采取更有意识的行动方式。但出人意料的是，那些选择深思熟虑的人，其表现反而不如那些依照习惯行事的人。

paragraphs.contentEn: Habits are not, therefore, the enemy of free will. In fact, they can make life easier. The downside of habits appears when they stop serving our goals. Bad habits push us towards choices that undermine what we really want. People who are trying to lose weight, for example, often struggle against long-standing eating habits that favour unhealthy options. Staying on track in these moments often requires strong, sustained willpower to resist the pull of old habits. When we are distracted, stressed or fatigued it is harder to counteract our bad habits. Even brief dips in motivation can prompt lapses into our old ways, kickstarting a chain of negative emotions, denting our confidence in our ability to change, and so unravelling our efforts to change our behaviour.
paragraphs.contentZh: 所以说，习惯并不是自由意志的敌人。相反，习惯能让日常生活变得更轻松。只有当习惯不再服务于我们的目标时，它的负面作用才会显现。不良习惯会将我们引向那些违背自己真正意愿的选择。比如，想要减肥的人常常需要与自己根深蒂固的饮食习惯对抗（这些习惯往往倾向于选择不健康的食物）。要在这种情况下保持自律，通常需要强大而持久的意志力来抵抗旧习惯的牵引。而当我们分心、压力过大或感到疲惫时，抵御不良习惯的能力就会下降。哪怕只是片刻的动力下滑，也可能让我们重新陷入旧有模式，进而触发连锁的负面情绪，削弱我们对改变的信心，并让此前为改变所付出的努力逐渐瓦解。

paragraphs.contentEn: Effective ways to break bad habits include identifying and avoiding triggers to unwanted habits, and making unwanted behaviour harder to automatically activate. A habitual evening snacker might, for example, avoid going to the kitchen in the evening so that they aren’t tempted by the snack cupboard. Our findings show that habits play a huge role in shaping our everyday lives, often helping us act efficiently. Understanding how habits work provides a powerful tool for behaviour change. Whether you are making a new routine or breaking an old one, recognising the triggers that drive your actions – and how you respond to them – can help you stay in control.
paragraphs.contentZh: 改掉不良习惯的有效方法包括：识别并避开会触发不良行为的情境，以及增加不良行为执行的难度，使其难以被无意识激活。比如，习惯在晚上吃零食的人，可以选择晚上不进厨房，从而避免暴露在零食柜的诱惑之下。我们的研究结果表明，习惯在塑造我们的日常生活中起着重要作用，很多时候能够帮助我们更高效地行动。理解习惯的运作机制，是实现行为改变的有力工具。无论你是想养成新习惯，还是摆脱旧习惯，学会识别驱动你行为的触发因素——并觉察自己如何对其作出反应——都能够帮助你重新掌握生活的主动权。
